<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD defines standard sources, including a tarball from the project's official GitHub repository tagged at a specific version (v1.120), along with two local files (koboldcpp.desktop and koboldcpp.png). The `sha256sums` array provides valid checksums for all sources, indicating an intention to verify integrity, though even if they were 'SKIP', that would not make this stage unsafe.

During `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare`, the only executable portions are the top-level PKGBUILD parsing and any `pkgver()` function (which is absent here). There is no `pkgver()` function, so no dynamic version calculation occurs. All variables are statically defined, and there is no command substitution or immediate execution in the global scope. The `source` array uses a direct HTTPS link to a trusted upstream (GitHub.com/LostRuins/koboldcpp), and no `git clone` with mutable refs or runtime fetches are involved at this stage.

Therefore, sourcing the PKGBUILD and downloading the sources poses no risk of arbitrary code execution or data exfiltration during this narrow phase.
</details>

No dynamic code execution during source fetch and parse
</summary>

The sources point to the official upstream project, and checksums are provided and valid.
